newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades steady at 3.00/3.03 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades steady at 3.00/3.03 pct.

text.p: German call money traded mostly unchanged at 3.00/3.03 percent on Thursday, indicating liquidity conditions were generally in equilibrium.

Dealers said they did not expect significant changes in the coming sessions as banks' holdings at the Bundesbank were sufficient for the moment. Therefore banks will likely not need to scramble for funds before the weekend, a dealer said.
Trading was mostly thin today, they added.
The Bundesbank is expected to keep rates unchanged at its meeting today and announce another fixed repo at three percent.
"We have enough funds and should be able to end the week without any significant rate swings," a dealer said.

While interest rates are unlikely to be changed today, dealers still harbour some hope the central bank may announce that it will free repurchase agreements from the reserve requirement. German banks have long demanded this step as reserve requirements on such short-term financing have led many banks to conduct such business abroad, hurting the German financial market. The Bundesbank has indicated it may consider a change as part of its ongoing efforts to help improve conditions in the German market.

Banks held 39.6 billion marks at the Bundesbank on Wednesday, down from 40.4 billion marks. The monthly average however remains unchanged at 39.4 billion marks. Lombard borrowings totalled 100 million marks on Wednesday.
On Thursday the Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.04000 percent compared with 3.04200 percent a day earlier.
